name: flickr_scraper
what_it_holds: Python Flickr image scraper (298 stars) for building keyword-based image sets via the Flickr API, with pagination and deduplication; not geotag-specific but Flickr API responses include geo fields when present.
why_useful: Could be adapted to pull geotagged Flickr photos for specific tourism-city keywords/date ranges as a rough photo-volume travel proxy, though it is a general scraper rather than a tourism-purpose-built tool and would need location filtering added.
themes: Twitter/X, Instagram, Flickr, TikTok tourism datasets: geotagged tourism flows, YFCC100M tourism subsets, Foursquare/Gowalla/Brightkite check-ins

name: swarm-to-sqlite
what_it_holds: Tool (67 stars) that exports a user's own Foursquare Swarm check-in history into a local SQLite database via the Foursquare API.
why_useful: Only works for a single authenticated user's own history, not a bulk tourism dataset -- flagged for completeness as a Foursquare-adjacent acquisition method but not directly useful at panel scale.

name: GDELT-GKG-Themes
what_it_holds: A committed CSV enumerating all known GDELT Global Knowledge Graph (GKG) theme codes (the taxonomy GDELT uses to tag articles, e.g. TOURISM, ECON_*, WB_*, TAX_* categories). Small reference file, not event data itself.
why_useful: Needed as a lookup table to filter GDELT GKG output for travel/tourism/hospitality/regulatory themes without guessing theme-code strings; a small but genuinely useful piece of plumbing for any GDELT-based nowcast.
themes: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers
why_all: Needed as a lookup table to filter GDELT GKG output for travel/tourism/hospitality/regulatory themes without guessing theme-code strings; a small but genuinely useful piece of plumbing for any GDELT-based nowcast.

name: Eventdb-Validity-Audit
what_it_holds: Fully reproducible (R + Python) measurement-validity audit comparing four political-event databases (GDELT, ICEWS, Phoenix, Tsinghua) against a hand-built 712-event gold standard; finds GDELT tracks 'trade' events well but not 'opinion' events (Phoenix does opinion better). Includes the gold-standard dataset and comparison code.
why_useful: Not travel-specific, but directly relevant methodology if the team ever builds a GDELT-based news/event nowcast for ABNB: it is documented evidence of which event categories GDELT is and isn't reliable for, which should inform how much weight to put on a GDELT-derived signal.
time_coverage: gold standard sample period unspecified in listing, repo active as of 24 Aug 2026
size_hint: 712-event hand-coded gold standard + 4 event-DB comparison extracts
